item.title: Re: Admin Panel
item.content:encoded:
Well, while this idea is indeed fascinating I feel like it's missing something. Personally, I think the best SCPs have a balance of power, advantages, disadvantages, ups and downs. This one is just ups, it is all powerful, was easily found and taken, easily controlled. It was so smooth it was a bit boring.
I think it needs some twists to balance it out. For example, if you change one setting another one changes too in order to even things out (you increase the gravity and the density of things decrease, for example), or only people of specific faith can use and be affected by it, or you have limited "points" to use to make the changes. Those are some quick ideas, you can think of something more elaborate.
There is potential here but it still needs some work. I hope you find the perfect balance to make it successful!

item.title: Admin Panel
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article (with ACS)

Genre (Optional ): Science-Fiction

Page Layout (Optional ): Classic SCP styling with logs on how far down researchers have dug into the program.

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is essentially the admin panel of the local universe, for example, the ability to explore the universe in a single program along with "editing", usually being extremely sophisticated (To the Planck scale)

Addtional details
Hide

Central Narrative: After a world-wide phenomenon wherein the gravity of Earth significantly increased, the foundation investigated the "source" of the phenomenon rumored to be at an abandoned facility, locals claiming that said facility suddenly appeared 2 days ago. The facility was empty, but investigators found a computer alien to Human-made devices. Upon opening the computer, it was found to contain only one program, named "בְּרִיאָה IIV", translated from Hebrew: "Creation".

After bringing the computer to a foundation site, the program was put into testing, showing a 3-d map of the universe, with the ability to "edit" certain aspects of it. The map can be fast-forwarded. Upon selecting earth, it has been seen that gravity was set to "1.0294 G", assumed to be an imperfection after the gravity change 2 days prior. After setting gravity to exactly 1, people reported "feeling some sort of lesser weight", with it reported to be extremely mild.

After scrolling down ~5 meters, investigators noticed that the program has the ability to manipulate the amount of intelligence a species has. The "Cognitive Factor" for humans was set to 0.00109, apes having their CF being at 0.0084. Investigators set the CF of "Canis lupus familiaris" (dogs) at 0.0079 from the value 0.00204. 2 weeks later, a dog was reported to be able to communicate in morse after a researcher decided to teach a dog international morse code, stating that it was to test if said program worked after hearing of the incident and the dog intelligence change.

Lastly, a notable ability of the program is to change the laws of physics themselves. Formulas of every aspect of physics are editable, known or unknown, including gravity, laws of motion, etc.
The SCP can edit and create, such as astronomical phenomena, time, and the very foundations of physics, all branches of it.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The SCP is God's Program. Stolen, tweaked, then contained.

Additional Notes: Would be nice to get tips for a lot more features.

item.title: Re: A helping hand (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
3) For comparison, "mage hand" is a spell in D&D that is limited to moving at a walking speed and has a carry limit of 5 pounds; it's a basic spell.

When it comes to firearms, I wasn't worried about it being able to carry them so much as being able to deal with the blast of the firearm itself. In essence, just because it can carry a pistol doesn't mean it can fire one. Note that most assault rifles are under 15 pounds, but again there's an issue of whether or not it could handle the thrust caused by firing it.

4) Most SCPs naturally avoid social media; they either happen far outside of its influence or have some sort of natural obfuscatory property that keeps them out of the social media spotlight. That's why you don't see a lot of clear pictures of most anomalies. My concern is that the helping hand may be too obvious. But that's a minor point; it could just appear too quickly to get a good picture of it.

Good luck with this; you might want to PM some of the Butterfly Squad to see if they will greenlight it.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Kiwi14! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It's nice to see people who have been interested in all-things-SCP finally join our ~official~ place on the internet. After all, here, you can affect the quality of works by voting and contributing yourself - speaking of which, it's really nice to see you so interested in writing some things - I can't wait to see what you come up with!

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Re: A Bio-Mechanical structure that can replicate the SCPF universe as a "Wiki".
item.content:encoded:
1) Right off the bat, you need to define what form the structure takes and what connection The Foundation has to it. "Structure" is way too vague, considering that while the assumption would be some sort of building, any artificial construction from a cell phone to an RV would qualify. Also, there's no obvious connection to The Foundation that needs to be better delineated.

2) It can't be infinitely recursive. While it's a neat story construct, there are memory limitations even for anomalous structure. It's ultimately just a paradoxical construct that has no good reason for existing, and as such needs to be dropped from the concept. The proper hook is that it's something that proves that the universe is a work of fiction and it needs to be approached as such.

3) Going back to you need to define the structure better: If it can be used to edit reality, then you need to better how it edits reality. Saying that it can edit reality really does no hood; you need to better define that particular aspect. While you're at it, why it hasn't been abused should make for an interesting topic.

4) All of that said, I'm not sure about having an anomaly that lays bare the meta-fictional nature of the universe really does anything. It just feels wonky, especially with how ill-defined this is.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: The Mechanical General
item.content:encoded:
1) I'm really not sure what you're trying to accomplish with this. There just seems to be some sort of theme missing here. If you were trying to make a point about war it's lost because there is just no connection with anyone real, and the whole "coming from a different dimension" just further separates him from anyone else. The best you have is "war is universal", but it just comes across as "meh" here.

2) The bodily fluids being excreted just seems gratuitous. Again, if there were some sort of theme here it would work, but it just seems like you're adding in shock value just for the sake of adding shock value. Something has obviously taken care to create this person, and adding those kinds of features just doesn't make any kind of functional sense.

3) The bottom line is that you have all of this technology and it just isn't paying off for you because there is no reason for it. It just feels all sorts of random, and that the general is stuck on repeat really doesn't help. There either has to be a way to get him past that point or otherwise figure out what happened to the guy or else it just feels like a random anomaly of some sort.

You just need some sort of unifying theme here.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: SCP Idea: The Mechanical General

item.title: Re: Modern Revival of an Age-Old Industry
item.content:encoded:
You have some serious issues to work through here.

1) The poachers would be easy to determine; if they were in a show, their identities would be determined by the second commercial break. Also, whale oil hasn't been a product for over a century; it doesn't burn as clean as kerosene. I'm not sure there would be a market for it; even those looking for more eco-friendly products would have a problem using a whale-based product. The flesh, however, would be a major product, especially in Japan.

2) The other major issue is that right whales are kept an eye on. If more than a dozen or two disappeared from the same area someone would be notified and you would see a lot more than a patrol boat looking for them. You may also want to pare down the catch for another reason: Not only is it hard to harvest that much whale, but that much whale product coming to market would raise a few eyebrows. Yeahyeah I know: Pesky reality issues. But if the horror is too from reality it just stops being taken seriously.

3) The real mystery is where they got the teleportation gear from. Especially gear that works that badly. That's the question you really need to answer.

item.title: The Hinterland Division (How many apocalypses could there be?)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article, Tale, Site Dossier, Other (It is a combination of all the previous ones using a hub page)

Elevator Pitch: The O5 council creates a new staff classification with O5 security clearance that works under direct orders of the O5 to allow them to have more staff at their disposal for operations that couldn't be told about to those with a lower security level. An agent at the Foundation is promoted to this new staff designation and is assigned to watch over an O5 level security project designed to stop end of the world scenarios from happening.

Central Narrative: In light of several new SCP discoveries that could lead to end of the world scenarios the O5 council decides that methods need to be made for dealing with problems like these, so they make a new project and promote the most reliable agent they have to a recently made position which grants him O5 level clearance. He’s assigned to spearhead the project, creating his own team and coming up with methods to then test and hopefully find the best method to deal with every SCP object or threat, reporting everything he’s doing directly to the council. There will be SCP’s referenced and it will also include several that I’m coming up with.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think that the incorporation of an character who is overseeing the files being the one who you are in the perspective of is pretty unique and different from other things on the site as they mostly don’t give the reader a character.

Additional Notes: I have not nearly finished yet so I won't be posting the sandbox pages very soon as there is still a lot to figure out in terms of the story. I just want to know if the concept is good enough that I should continue it and I want to get greenlit earlier on so I don’t have to worry about it later, I’m not sure if this will need to be split into several drafts since the pages will inevitably have cross links to each other in them

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight for SCP (a.k.a The Golden Opportunity)
item.content:encoded:
If this was being done as more of a parody, I could see it. But you would need to have the kid shaken not suicidal, and maybe if the kid was a little older.

The problem is that Wonka is being presented as someone who is super freaky and creepy from the get-go, and that sets off a lot of alarms. Because the kid is being taken against his will and something is done to him that makes him suicidal, it just feels sort of cheap. If the victims weren't so young and you weren't presenting Wonka as "super-freaky" there would be less of a problem.

However, if you were presenting Wonka as more "over-zealous" and with some sort of agenda and the kid was not only older but was more of an evil kid after the experience, you may have something. Especially if the kid was more about manipulation than violence.

You just need to throw some sort of twist related to Wonka rather than just abusing some poor kid. While I don't mind seeing kids killed in horror (I blame 1980s horror movies!), my limit is seeing them hurt this specific way.

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight for SCP (a.k.a The Golden Opportunity)
item.content:encoded:
There have been issues brought to me about copyright and trash. It is possible to switch the character name.

I'm pretty certain that just swapping out names wouldn't properly address the fact that you're still just making an overly grimdark, edgy version of Willy Wonka and his Chocolate Factory.

I'll be honest, I personally would recommend scrapping this. Not only does the core premise rely heavily on existing copyrighted work, there are also a lot of gratuitous horror elements added in seemingly just to follow said copyrighted work. I myself as a reader would downvote pretty immediately for this:

Even though Willy is super freaky and creepy, at first the child is not frightened. But when they end up back at the house, they suffer from major PTSD until they either die of stress, malnourishment, or suicide.

It seems incredibly tasteless to write about an entity preying exclusively on children, including abducting them in a traumatic process, and causing their death. Suicide and child abuse are already difficult to write tactfully; the way these plot elements have been handled currently does not convince me that the piece would be workable no matter how many edits you make to it.

I highly recommend that you write something else.

item.title: Re: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.content:encoded:
Special Containment Procedures: SCP-5459 is to be kept in a 5x5 meter box at all times. No one is to enter the box unless a controlled testing is taking place. 2 armed guards are to be stationed around the box and containment area, rotating every 20 hours. Anyone who is tested, or has been within 20m of SCP-5459 has to undergo a psych brief and debrief, and a day quarantine. SCP-5459 is able to enter others' minds and cause intense emotional distress if in an enraged state. SCP-5459 is agitated and enraged if more than 3 people are in his box. He will stay in normal form if calm, and if enraged may attempt to telepathically confuse others to get himself out or to harm others. Anyone who's mind has been entered by SCP-5459 are to be quarantined for seven (7) days.1 In the event of a containment breach, all personnel are advised to not approach within 20m of SCP-5459 to avoid getting controlled or enraging SCP-5459. If SCP-5459 is needed to be approached, a *maximum* of 2 personnel may approach. Any Class-D attempting to approach SCP-5459 in a containment breach must be terminated.

This made me infuriated, frustrated, and powerless.

It reminded me a LOT of when I fought tooth and nail for over a year to get my insurance to cover my medication - nothing but bureaucracy, bad faith, and endless and awfu-

Gah, just thinking back on it is making my blood pressure rise.

… +1 for writing something that's good enough to elicit that kind of response.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Salutations. Long time, first time. I plan to read and possibly vote and offer feedback. I've been away from this site for a while. When I came back, there was a Series 6! I thought to myself, "hey, you mostly stick to old, proven works, why not jump into new stuff?" So I did. Then I thought, "if you really like some of these articles, why not join so you can offer some feedback?" And now I'm writing this.

"When is the last time it rained?" I've never experienced a drought nor do I live in an area where droughts really happen. Nevertheless, when that thought pops into my mind I have to try and figure out the last time there was rainfall or I cannot sleep.

item.title: Re: How many greenlight requests am I allowed to make per week?
item.content:encoded:
Assuming that by "greenlight requests" you mean "concept threads", the Ideas Critique required reading states: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13282684/required-reading:how-to-use-this-forum-ideas

Each author is limited to posting two new concept threads per week (every 7 days).

Please note that if an author is posting an excessive number of new threads, staff may order them to slow down and only post material that they are willing to work on, rather than posting and quickly discarding.

item.title: Re: ""Bureaucracy""
item.content:encoded:
I pretty much 100% agree with all of this. It entirety reminds me of an SCP whose number escapes me at the moment, where the Foundation purposely gives WWS a hard-to-contain anomaly to bankrupt it and remove it from the ecosystem. I feel like this would work much better as a WWS format than anything else; where the reader's perspective is placed in the plucky group dealing with the bloated bureaucracy, rather than the bloated bureaucracy itself.
